findings.description: getStream FD guard leak fix — exit path audit
findings.fix_sketch: N/A — review only; all exit paths are covered.

findings.description: Double-release guard: `cleanedUp` flag prevents `release()` and `fileHandle.close()` from being called more than once across all exit paths (pull end, pull error, cancel, abandon timer)

Guard entry release via `release()` call inside `cleanup()` — confirmed on all four stream exit paths: pull end-of-stream (line 357), pull error (line 369), cancel (line 374), abandon timer (line 327-334)
File handle close via `fileHandle.close().catch(() => {})` inside `cleanup()` — confirmed on all four stream exit paths
Abandon timer (60s, unref'd) provides safety net for the 'never read, never cancelled' case — forces cleanup and logs a warning

Pre-existing minor issue: if `fileHandle.stat()` throws after `fsp.open()` succeeded (line 311), the outer catch (line 377) calls `release()` but `fileHandle.close()` is never called because the `cleanup` closure is defined after line 312. File descriptor is leaked. This is not part of the FD guard leak fix — it is a pre-existing condition that existed before the fix.
findings.fix_sketch: Move lines 315-323 (cleanedUp/cleanup) before lines 311-312 (open/stat), or add a separate `fileHandle.close()` in the outer catch block.
